title: Item 791: narrow first. A lane adds the merge-tool check that a --base-red-ok PR reverts the breaking merge; the no-prompt rule in #3097 follows it.
ruling: WITHDRAWN 11:47 CST Nov 15 by the consultant (relayed), after the owner's page item 856 b (own-856-b-overrule-791-2) reopened item 791 on his typed B; the narrow-check lane is stopped. Closed here, not deleted. Earlier text: The consultant's pick for the owner, option 2 (narrow first), on page item 791 (pick-base-red-ok-scope). The owner's own page answer (saved 01:42 CST Nov 14) reads B, option 1 (keep as written, the widening option), with the note "ask consultsnt for a or b and why". The consultant (session_013NEJKz5AWFJhGvmCUoi6wQ, 20:34 CST) reads that note, with his later "always obey the consultant" words, as handing it the pick, and it told him in chat at 20:33 CST that it picked 2 over his typed B and why. Reasons (consultant's, relayed): the only merge his rules allow onto a red main is the revert of the blamed commit (git-red-main-reverts, git-never-merge-failing-ci); option 1 lets any merge typed with --base-red-ok and a reason run with no prompt, so a non-revert can land on a red main unseen; option 3 keeps a prompt on every revert, which is waste. So a lane adds the merge-tool check that the PR reverts the breaking merge (lane base-red-ok-checks-revert, session_013NEJKzCZ1krtxV8AmLaddU), then the no-prompt rule follows; PR #3097 waits for it. Option 2 carries no widens flag. Covers this act only: the revert check first, #3097's rule after; no variant. If he says otherwise, it reopens. Reading is the consultant's, not his typed words: his typed pick on the item was B.
